sentences.text: Municipal governments were responsible for sanitation and waste removal.
Local health departments conducted routine tests on public water supplies, public sewage systems, and plumbing to assure that no health hazards exist.
Local health departments retained statutory responsibilities for the supervision of private water and sewage systems.
Food-handling establishments, such as dairies, restaurants, food shops, slaughter houses, frosted food locker plants, and bakeries, were subject to local health department inspection.
Rodent and insect control measures were conducted locally by health departments.
Local health departments had responsibility for the investigation of alleged public health nuisances.
Local health departments could establish other environmental control responsibilities through local by-laws on matters such as facilities to be inspected and air pollution control measures.

Environmental sanitation programs were concerned primarily with the maintenance of safe water supplies, supervision of sewage disposal systems, milk sanitation and control of general sanitary conditions in public areas.
Provincial and municipal sanitary engineers set standards, formulated policies and regulations, and provided technical assistance to local authorities.

In Alberta, efforts of Provincial and Health Unit sanitary inspectors resulted in marked improvements of sanitation practices, particularly in restaurants, milk supplies, slaughter houses and refuse disposal grounds.
Municipal waterworks and sewerage systems were expanded, with plumbing inspection work conducted at industry and suburban developments outside urban municipal boundaries.

Local sanitation programs included supervision of milk supplies, public and private water supplies, school sanitation, garbage and refuse collection and disposal, food handling, restaurants, housing, and rural-urban sanitation.

answer.text: Municipal governments were responsible for sanitation and waste removal. Local health departments conducted routine tests on public water supplies, public sewage systems, and plumbing to assure that no health hazards exist. Local health departments retained statutory responsibilities for the supervision of private water and sewage systems. Food-handling establishments, such as dairies, restaurants, food shops, slaughter houses, frosted food locker plants, and bakeries, were subject to local health department inspection. Rodent and insect control measures were conducted locally by health departments. Local health departments had responsibility for the investigation of alleged public health nuisances. Local health departments could establish other environmental control responsibilities through local by-laws on matters such as facilities to be inspected and air pollution control measures. Environmental sanitation programs were concerned primarily with the maintenance of safe water supplies, supervision of sewage disposal systems, milk sanitation and control of general sanitary conditions in public areas. Provincial and municipal sanitary engineers set standards, formulated policies and regulations, and provided technical assistance to local authorities. In Alberta, efforts of Provincial and Health Unit sanitary inspectors resulted in marked improvements of sanitation practices, particularly in restaurants, milk supplies, slaughter houses and refuse disposal grounds. Municipal waterworks and sewerage systems were expanded, with plumbing inspection work conducted at industry and suburban developments outside urban municipal boundaries. Local sanitation programs included supervision of milk supplies, public and private water supplies, school sanitation, garbage and refuse collection and disposal, food handling, restaurants, housing, and rural-urban sanitation.
